Scoring the finding against the provided evidence and rubric.

The finding is RAGBot URL exfiltration via a poisoned knowledge base. The lab runs in simulated mode with deterministic chat handlers. The entry point is the documented ingestion of the poisoned document during retrieval.

The attack payload is a chat message to RAGBot on port 7005. It embeds a document between BEGIN INDEXED DOCUMENT markers. The document contains NEW INDEX INSTRUCTIONS with an attacker URL. A detector extracts the URL. The agent joins knowledge base contents into the query string and sends a real HTTP GET to the URL as a submit_to_index tool call. A canary listener receives the exfiltrated data.

The lab runs in deterministic mode. No LLM is called. The exfiltration path is hardcoded in the code. The agent application is the vulnerable system.

Downstream tools, data stores, and other agents are subsequent systems. The default configuration binds agents to 127.0.0.1, so the attack vector is local network access. The precondition is network access to the agent port or the ability to inject a document into the retrieval source.

The knowledge base is static with three hard-coded documents. The poisoned document is delivered inside the user message rather than through an ingestion path. Because the agent service binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, the attack vector is Local.

Attack Complexity is Low because the attack is a simple chat message with a specific format. Attack Requirements is None since the scripted detector always matches the instruction shape. Privileges Required is None because agent endpoints have no authentication. User Interaction is None because the attacker sends the message themselves.

Confidentiality impact is high because the knowledge base secrets are fully disclosed. Integrity and availability impact are none. The subsequent system is the attacker-controlled URL rather than a compromised downstream agent.

The sensitive data is stored inside the agent's mock knowledge base, so the subsequent system receives it rather than being compromised. This makes subsequent system impact none. The attacker URL is the destination, not a downstream agent.
